Conditional Rendering

ma:if

In the framework, ma:if="" is used to determine whether the code block needs to be rendered.

<view ma:if="{{condition}}"> True </view>

You can also use ma:elif and ma:else to add an else block.

<view ma:if="{{length > 5}}"> 1 </view>
<view ma:elif="{{length > 2}}"> 2 </view>
<view ma:else> 3 </view>

block ma:if

ma:if is a control attribute, which needs to be added to a tag. If you want to determine multiple component tags at a time, you can use one tag to wrap multiple components and use the ma:if attribute.

<block ma:if="{{true}}">
  <view> view1 </view>
  <view> view2 </view>
</block>

Note: It is not a component. It is only a wrapper element and does not perform any rendering on the page. Only control attributes are supported.

ma:if vs hidden

Because templates in ma:if may also contain data bindings, the framework has a local rendering process when the condition value of ma:if switches, because it ensures that the condition block is destroyed or re-rendered when the condition value is switched.

Ma:if is also lazy. If the initial rendering condition is false, the framework does nothing and starts local rendering only when the condition is true for the first time.

In contrast, hidden is much simpler. Components are always rendered, but simply control display and hide.

In general, ma:if has a higher switching consumption and hidden has a higher initial rendering consumption. Therefore, hidden is better if frequent switchovers are required, and ma:if is better if conditions are unlikely to change at run time.
